First Rainbow Six Siege Expansion Delayed Slightly [Feb 2] (x-post /v/CoOpGaming)

I'd much prefer they fix the getting stuck and the not getting end of game experience/currency issues first before they release any expansions. That last one is really game breaking for me, at least the first one can be fixed by going prone.

I wonder if that might be the cause of the delays, to be honest. But in either case I agree. Rainbow Six: Siege is an excellent game that's only big issue is server problems. It's well-balanced, it's a tactical and compelling game, and it's got excellent replay value in its multiplayer. The problem is that it's currently experiencing persistent server issues, and that's a huge problem for a multiplayer-only game. I wouldn't be surprised if they put their DLC plans on the shelf to address the server issues first, and I certainly hope that's the case.

Kind of a tangent; is Ubisoft just shit at creating and optimizing network code? A lot of their games have severe server issues, and their Uplay/Ubisoft Club apps or websites take forever to load and are really unresponsive.
That could very well be the case. If so, it's something they'll definitely have to work on, because it's the only glaring issue with the game right now.

Separate response because I wanted to address the gameplay points. I've always been a huge fan of asymmetrical multiplayer gameplay, and this game delivers so well. I agree with pretty much all of your points.

No worries :) and I agree, the attack vs defense concept is executed perfectly. So much attention went into gameplay and balancing this game, which is why I want it to do well. Unfortunately having server issues right out of the gate hurts its popularity, so I hope Ubisoft mobilizes quickly on the network issues. If not, my fear is that the playbase will decline and Ubisoft will drop support for the game due to a drop in popularity. It really is sink or swim for Ubisoft on this one.

The good news is that they've invested a whole lot of time and money into this game, and I'm sure they recognize the potential success they have on their hands. Ubisoft has been dying to get into the "recurring multiplayer" kind of popularity that games like Call of Duty and Counter Strike have, and this might be their big chance to get their foot in that door. That gives me hope that they'll put the effort into this one and fix the server issues. They have a gem on their hands; they just need to polish it now.

I'm surprised by how good Siege is, honestly. When I first saw the reveal a few years back, it looked promising, like a return to the subdued and deliberate pace of classic R6 games that stressed planning and execution over twitch-shooting.

But when I saw livestreams of the closed alpha/betas, it looked pretty generic. I held on to hope that the people playing were just not used to the game, and played it like a straightup shooter.

It wasn't until I got into the open beta did I realize how special it really was. The full game is even better with all the different operatives to choose from, and generally speaking - Balance is pretty good too.

But the server issues... They're constantly fucking up. If Ubisoft can't keep them stable, this game is going to suffer big time. Especially if they want to push it as a competitive FPS.

Yeah, I was initially concerned about the lack of campaign, because co-op campaign is my favorite thing about Tom Clancy games, but Siege feels like a game that dropped campaign to focus on what they do well rather than a game that dropped campaign out of laziness. Good balancing, interesting gameplay, diverse characters, and a great destruction mechanic are all great assets. If they fix the server issues, this might end up being my most played game of 2016.
